reasoning: Set B has the better RL design and stays closer to the brief. Every environment gets both a random player and a scripted bot, the DQN and policy-gradient ladders are built one piece at a time, test seeds are held out, comparisons use 5 seeds with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, and the fish see far enough (radius 4, ball speed 2) to dodge. Its build layer, however, is broken. The M1 plan was not replanned after AD-16/AD-17 changed the core to sides and schedules. M1-T01 and M1-T03 read the retired `registry.make_agent`, so their context packets failed to generate, and one of them is the interface task that every other task waits on. PL-01's entry sketch calls `run_streams`, `make_agents` and `make_schedule`, and the step table includes `test_lineup` and `SoloSchedule`, but no M1 task builds any of them. The architecture still carries process narration ('On approval: pipeline-design updates PL-01–PL-03…'). Set A's design is weaker. There is no random baseline anywhere. It adds a rented-GPU budget, which the 'free tools only' constraint rules out. It also leaves its own flagged flaw unresolved: the ball comes into view only one step before contact, so fish can't dodge it. Twelve packages is over-split for a solo learner, and M4 is a probe-gated leftover milestone. Even so, A's M1 plan, contracts and packets agree, every packet generates, the interface task freezes typed boundaries with fakes, and the dependency graph is mostly sound. A builder can start on A today and cannot start on B, so A wins narrowly.
